case_name: Dharminder Singh @ Vijay Singh v State
respondent:
State
Supreme Court of India

12 August 2013
Cr.A. No. 1614 of 2010 with Cr.A. No. 1151 of 2013 (Arising out of S.L.P.(Cr.) No. 1939 of 2011)
(Non-Reportable)
The Judgment was delivered by : Ranjan Gogoi, J.
1. Leave granted in SLP (Crl.) No. 1939 of 2011.
Each of the appellants in the appeals under consideration have been convicted u/ss. 364 and 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code by the Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Rohini, Delhi. They have been sentenced to undergo RI for 10 years for the offence under Section 364/34 IPC whereas for the offence under Section 302/34 IPC they have been sentenced to undergo RI for life. Aggrieved, appellant Dharminder Singh @ Vijay Singh had filed Crl. A. No. 603/2008 and appellant Chintu Malhotra had filed Crl. A. No. 406/2008 before the High Court of Delhi. As the said appeals have been dismissed by the common order of the High Court dated 11.05.2009 appellant Dharminder Singh @ Vijay Singh has filed Crl
facts: The prosecution case is that on 26.08.2000 the accused-appellants alongwith two other co-accused had hired Maruti Van No. DL 3CR 1271 to go to Haridwar.

According to the prosecution, PW-4 Jitender Kumar was called by the deceased to Kaushik Travels to deliver fresh clothes and at the said place he had met the accused appellants, including accused Dharminder who is a friend of his brother Anirudh.
The same was later identified to be that of Krishan Kumar.
According to PW-4 accused appellant Dharminder was known to him from before as he is a friend of his elder brother, PW-8.
PW-24 SI Dal Chand had initially investigated the case.

From the evidence of PW-20 Insp. Kuldeep Singh it is evident that on 27.08.2000 an information was received at Police Station Jawalapur, Haridwar to the effect that the dead body of a male person was lying beneath the bridge at Ranipur Nahar.
issues: Whether the prosecution has conclusively proved the involvement of the accused in the alleged crime?
Whether the evidence of PW-4 is reliable and worthy of credence?
petitioner_arguments: The FIR registered at 2.30 P.M. on 29.8.2000 must be understood to be ante-dated inasmuch as the vehicle and the accused appellants were apprehended in Purnia only at 9.15 P.M of the said day.
No test identification parade was carried out and no recovery of weapons used in the alleged crime has been made by the prosecution.
A large number of witnesses vital to the prosecution case had turned hostile.
respondent_arguments: The evidence of PWs 4 and 8 clearly establish that the accused appellants had hired the vehicle driven by the deceased to go to Haridwar and on the very next morning the dead body of Krishan Kumar was recovered under the bridge from a place near Haridwar.
court_reasoning: The court has considered the arguments advanced by both sides and finds that the prosecution has failed to conclusively prove the involvement of the accused in the alleged crime.
The evidence of PW-4 is not reliable and worthy of credence due to certain serious infirmities inherent in it.
holding: The circumstances proved by the prosecution, in the absence of any reasonable explanation on the part of the accused, cannot give rise to any other conclusion except that it is the accused alone who had abducted deceased Krishan Kumar and had killed him at Haridwar.
